instructions: The night before: move 1 sheet of the puff pastry from the freezer to the fridge to thaw. Keep the other sheet frozen for another day.
Grate the Gruyère. That should be about 1 cup.
Unfold the pastry onto a sheet of plastic wrap and roll it out into a 10 by 12 inch rectangle.
Spread the 1 1/2 tbsp mustard over it, leaving a 1/2 inch strip bare along the long edge farthest from you.
Lay the ham over the mustard in an even layer, then sprinkle the Gruyère over the ham.
Starting from the long edge closest to you, roll it up tightly into a log and trim the ragged ends. Wrap it in the plastic wrap and chill it for 20 minutes. A soft log squashes when you slice it.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 375°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Line two baking sheets with parchment.
Cut the log into 1/2 inch slices with a serrated knife. That should be about 24. Lay them flat on the sheets about 1 inch apart.
Bake for about 18 minutes, swapping the sheets top to bottom halfway, until the pastry is light golden and the cheese is bubbling.
Let them cool on the sheets for 5 minutes. Serve warm or at room temperature.
advance_prep_notes: thaw the puff pastry in the fridge the night before
method_notes: All three versions spread mustard over a sheet of puff pastry, layer on deli ham and a melty cheese, roll it into a log, slice it and bake until golden. Well Plated (the lead) chills the log for 20 minutes before slicing it thin and bakes at 375°F; Lena's Kitchen brushes the slices with egg wash and seeds at 400°F, and Sustainable Cooks cuts thick rolls and bakes them close together in a dish under a seasoned butter. This is the lead at half the amount, one sheet for about 24 pinwheels, made with Gruyère and without the optional herbs.
